title: A Survey on Multilingual Large Language Models: Corpora, Alignment, and Bias

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model performance, representation quality, and sentiment prediction parity across different languages, specifically highlighting disparities between high-resource languages (like English) and low-resource languages.

Surveying multiple benchmarks (e.g., WEAT, Winogender, CrowS-Pairs) and masked language modeling prompts to measure stereotypical associations related to gender, race, religion, age, and occupation in word embeddings and sentence representations.
Evaluating whether models disproportionately favor Western-centric content, values, or concepts when processing and generating text for non-Western languages (such as Arabic).

Testing automated evaluation metrics (e.g., BERTScore) by feeding them sentences that differ only in demographic-associated names (e.g., phonology-gender associations) to detect biases within the metrics themselves.
